hooks.statusMessage: Checking whether this diff crosses hex boundaries
hooks.command: f=$(git diff --cached --name-only 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^src/main/java/net/vaier/.*\.java$' || true); [ -z "$f" ] && exit 0; l=$(printf '%s\n' "$f" | sed -nE 's#^src/main/java/net/vaier/(adapter/driven|application|domain|rest)/.*#\1#p' | sort -u | grep -c . || true); p=$(printf '%s\n' "$f" | grep -cE '(/domain/port/|Service\.java$|Adapter\.java$|UseCase\.java$)' || true); [ "$l" -ge 2 ] || [ "$p" -ge 1 ] || exit 0; printf '%s' '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"This staged diff engages the hex rules — it spans two or more layers, or touches a port / *Service / *Adapter / *UseCase. Run the hex-architecture-checker agent on it and confirm it is clean before committing: decisions in the domain (not service/controller/frontend); the domain owns port calls; services never call use cases; no *Service implements a driven For* port; a side-effect is NOT a use case, trigger it via a driven port; thin controllers. See the hexagonal-architecture skill. A single-layer diff with no port/Service/Adapter/UseCase does not reach this prompt — deliberately, so that the check means something when it does fire."}}'
